12 Agents Per Company, 50% Siloed: The Enterprise Agent Reality Check

By Will Zheng · April 13, 2026 · From Issue #6

Belitsoft / Google Cloud / Deloitte Industry

A major industry survey published this week found that the average enterprise now operates 12 AI agents — and half of them work in complete isolation, disconnected from other agents, systems, and workflows. The number is projected to reach 20 agents per company by 2027. AI agent priority among IT decision-makers jumped 31.5% year-over-year, with the highest deployment in cybersecurity, sales automation, customer service, and supply chain. But the deployment picture tells a story about where organizations actually are in this transition: agents are being stood up independently, by individual teams, solving local problems — without a shared architecture, shared memory, or shared understanding of how they connect. This is the enterprise equivalent of what Paul David documented about electrification: the tools are in the building, but the factory has not been redesigned around them. A single agent that drafts a client email is a productivity tool. An agent network where the CRM agent, the portfolio analysis agent, and the meeting prep agent share context and hand off seamlessly is something categorically different — and most organizations are nowhere near that. The 50% silos stat is not a failure. It's a baseline. The question is who builds the connective tissue first.
